evidence: The original workingTree() wrapped `git rev-parse` in `catch { /* no git / not a repo */ }`, so baseline.js's guessed 'not a git checkout?' replaced git's real stderr; 2ccdad2 removes the catches so git's error propagates, which is the reviewer's suggestion. The same change later cost F14, F16 and F19, because every caller now hard-requires git.
guidance_note: When a shared helper stops swallowing a failure, list every caller and decide for each whether it can live with the new hard requirement, before pushing.

evidence: The original run-case.js wrote findings.json first and meta.json last, while listRunDirs keys completeness on findings.json. The agent reordered the writes and renamed findings.json into place last instead of adding a try/catch, so the completion marker is true by construction. evidence: This duplicates F4: the same `estimateCandidateCostUsd(..., repeats)` call ignored the resume deficit. The same 2ccdad2 change fixed it.

evidence: The tree was snapshotted once and never checked against the runs produced in the same invocation, so the premise holds. guidance_note: When reusing an existing predicate for a new check, restate the question the new check asks (here 'did the tree move' vs 'is this provably mine') and test the new call site on the input class the old predicate rejects wholesale (dirty trees).

evidence: 2ccdad2 made workingTree() throw on any git failure. That turned a contended `git status` index lock across concurrent lanes, previously caught, into a fatal replay abort. The agent rightly kept the hard requirement (a null identity would seed refused runs) and fixed the real regression with `--no-optional-locks`. The comment's claim that 'every caller needs git for more than this' stays loose for run-case.js.
guidance_note: When a helper starts propagating errors, list the concurrent call sites and the transient failures they can now die on (index lock contention), and harden the read in the same commit.

narrative: A resume-across-quota-walls feature for the eval gate took five reviewed rounds plus one round-cap round. Round 1 was dominated by consequences of round-0 fixes: removing workingTree's error swallowing made git mandatory everywhere (F14/F16/F19), the cost-estimate change left three stale descriptions (F22/F24/F26), and reusing foreignRuns for the drift check broke every dirty-tree gate after paid replay (F18, S5). Rounds 2 and 3 were mostly doc-mirror misses: the README was fixed but not USAGE, or the README but not eval.yml. One partial hoist of the stale-verdict removal (F32→F36) made round 3 entirely fix-caused. The agent's F19 pushback was wrong, and F39 in round 4 forced the very change F19 pointed at.
guidance_observations: The round-0 summary's out-of-diff findings (README:218, README:487) were ignored and came back inline in round 1 as F20/F21, costing a round's worth of threads for work already requested.

Several fixes changed a shared helper or a documented behavior without grepping for its other callers and mirrored descriptions; a per-fix 'grep the old wording and the changed symbol' sweep would have prevented F22, F33→F38 and F37.
Reusing an existing predicate (foreignRuns) for a semantically different check produced the PR's only S5; a test of the new call site on dirty input before pushing would have caught it.
